guitar.evidence: Freddie King is well documented as primarily playing a Gibson ES-345 (and earlier Les Paul Goldtops) with a National fingerpick and thumbpick technique; a blues guitar icon.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown; well-established blues history fact.

tone.target: hot blues lead with biting midrange crunch
tone.profile: hot blues lead with biting midrange crunch
tone.summary: A vintage tube breakup chain using OD 9 for initial bite, followed by the UK 45 amp model with a UK Vintage 4x12 to deliver hot, focused blues lead tones.

rig.name: Freddie King - The Stumble - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum.
Provide initial grit and bite (tweed/Plexi emulation) without excessive fuzz.
Used as a secondary grit boost if OD 9 is insufficient, but kept low to avoid metal saturation.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style might be too aggressive; keep it mostly bypassed or set very low for subtle crunch.

blocks.purpose: Optional filter sweep for blues phrasing; kept off by default.
blocks.gap: Not essential for the core tone, but useful for expressive lead work.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the punchy, midrange-focused sound of a classic British blues amp (Plexi style).
Provide the classic British cabinet voicing and tight low end.
Fine-tune the midrange punch and bite required for hot blues lead.
Optional subtle thickening for sustained bends; kept off to maintain dryness.
blocks.gap: The target tone is dry and immediate, so this module is mostly bypassed.

blocks.purpose: Minimal slapback/echo for depth; kept very subtle to avoid 'echo-heavy space'.
blocks.gap: The verdict emphasizes dryness, so this is set minimally.

blocks.purpose: Provide a small-room live mono feel without sounding overly wet or spacious.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the raw, biting midrange crunch of hot blues leads.

proposals.reason: Better captures the raw, biting midrange and grit of classic blues.
